facts.fact: Chathu's deadline: if the account is still open at the new moon, nine nights from the morning of chapter 20, he sends Vellan.
facts.why: needed because the beat requires Ammu to warn that Vellan comes at the new moon; a count anchors it inside the 15-night window.

facts.fact: Ammu follows Neela's scent to the cache under the second spur at dawn and promises to write nothing to Chathu for one week; she will leave a reed in the cup on the seventh night.
facts.why: needed because the beat gives Ammu a one-week reprieve and a mechanism to meet again.

facts.fact: Old tappers' song verse: 'Tap the bark when the sun goes low, / let the black sap run and the lantern burn slow. / What the dusk has taken, the dusk will say, / the name given back at the closing of day.' Neela has never heard the last verse.
facts.why: needed because the beat requires a sung verse about 'the name given back'; invented wording.

facts.fact: Gopan taught Devan at sixteen to hold a river pebble in the cheek on long cistern watches so a sleeper cannot form clean words. From chapter 20 Devan keeps one in his cheek every night Neela smears resin, from dusk until she is back at first light.
facts.why: needed because the beat requires the old watchman's pebble trick.

facts.fact: Ammu believes Neela's lie that Devan does not know what she is.
facts.why: needed to show the second lie in the cost ledger and keep Ammu's report threat plausible.
